Companies can rent a partner tent at the race venue for team spirit and exposure through Rent a Tent. E2C was title partner for the fourth year in the 2024 edition.

name: VSM terräng
description: The Swedish Cross Country Championships are organised by Västerås FK and the Swedish Athletics Federation at Rocklunda IP in Västerås. The course is 2 km long and consists mostly of grass, with some other surfaces, including fast-running grass and gravel paths. The competition includes several categories, including seniors, youth, masters and para-athletes, with individual races and team competitions. The event also offers the option of pre-booked lunch and good accommodation options close to the venue.
course_highlights: 2 km course consisting mostly of grass, with some other surfaces
Fast-running grass and a 2–3-metre-wide gravel path, crossed four times per lap
Hay-bale obstacles on parts of the course
additional: Race numbers must be collected at the start/finish area at least 60 minutes before the start. Access to the start area opens 10 minutes before the start and closes 2 minutes before. Water is available at the lap point and finish, with Dextrosol at the finish. Changing rooms and showers are available at Expandia Arena. Free parking and local buses are available. Clubs may set up their own tents in the designated area. Pre-booked lunch is served at Good Morning Hotels near the venue. Doping tests may be conducted during the competition weekend. The 2026 event took place at Rocklunda IP in Västerås. The organiser’s website states that Västerås FK handed over hosting duties for the 2027 Swedish Cross Country Championships to Mora.

name: Linghem Dark Halfyard (Ultra) Trail
description: Welcome to the second edition of Linghem Dark Halfyard (Ultra) Trail, a unique and exciting running event in the autumn darkness of Kråksångsskogen. The race consists of 13 laps on a 3.5 km loop, with a maximum of 30 minutes allowed for each lap. After the sixth lap, runners change direction, adding an extra dimension to the competition. This is a small-scale race with a limited number of places, and a headlamp is mandatory because almost the entire race takes place in the dark. All participants who complete at least one lap receive a beautiful wooden medal, and the winners receive unique winner’s medals.
course_highlights: 13 laps on a 3.5 km loop, with a maximum of 30 minutes per lap
Running direction changes after the sixth lap
The course is marked with reflective markers and trail tape; the surface is mostly trails, with approximately 700 metres of gravel
additional: Energy is served during laps 7 and 8 (pizza from a local pizzeria), along with sweets, bananas, crisps, coffee, hot broth, sports drink and water. Facilities are very limited, with self-service energy, a warm fire and approximately 25 sq m of covered shelter. Toilets are outdoors in the forest. Maximum 70 places. Each lap starts every 30 minutes, and anyone who completes a lap faster can rest for the remaining time before the next lap starts. A headlamp and mobile phone are listed as mandatory equipment. The race website lists 70 places.

name: Halloween Night Trail
location: Friluftscentrum Karlsnäs, Ronneby, Blekinge County, Sweden
description: Halloween Night Trail is an exciting night trail race in the Karlsnäs area north of Ronneby, with distances of 2 km, 5 km and 10 km. The race offers a unique Halloween atmosphere, with themed features such as Zombie Hill, Count Dracula’s abode and the Bat Cave along the course. The event venue is at Friluftscentrum Karlsnäs, where the finish is indoors. After the race, grilled hamburgers and drinks are served and included in the entry fee. The race is organised by Ronneby Orienteering Club, which has extensive experience organising major orienteering competitions.
course_highlights: Run along small trails and through terrain, with reflectors showing the way in the dark
Themed features such as Zombie Hill, the Cemetery, Count Dracula’s abode and the Bat Cave
The finish area is indoors at Karlsnäs outdoor recreation centre
additional: Electronic timing for 5 km and 10 km; no timing for 2 km. Race bibs and chips can be collected at the venue from 17:00. The awards ceremony is provisionally scheduled for 20:45. Shoes with good grip and a headlamp are recommended. Parents can run with children in the 2 km race without registering. All participants receive a specially designed medal. The entry fee includes a hamburger and a drink. Electronic timing is offered for the 5 km and 10 km races, but not the 2 km race. The finish area is indoors.

name: Yddingeloppet
description: Yddingeloppet is one of Skåne’s largest cross-country races, held in the beautiful and challenging terrain of Bokskogen, Torup, outside Malmö. The race always takes place on the last Sunday in October, with the start and finish at Torups Friluftsgård. There are recreational classes over 6 km and 12 km, as well as a 6 km walking/pole-walking event, and competitive classes for different age groups and veteran classes. All participants receive a race bib with a timing chip and a medal at the finish. Prizes are awarded to the top finishers in the competitive classes, and winners in the veteran classes have their prizes mailed to them.
course_highlights: Cross-country race in Bokskogen, Torup, beautiful in autumn
Two distances: 6 km and 12 km
Start and finish at Torups Friluftsgård
additional: Race bibs with timing chips are provided to all participants except those in the walking and pole-walking events. Race bibs can be collected at the office during the week before the race or on race day from 8:30 a.m. until one hour before the start. The awards ceremony for places 1–3 in the 6 km and 12 km women’s and men’s competitive classes is at approximately 12:30 p.m. The start and finish area has parking and good public transport connections via buses 150 and 148. Carpooling is recommended. The race has previously been held in late October.

name: Sjögarpslunken 2026
description: Sjögarpslunken is a longstanding running race celebrating its 50th anniversary in 2026. The race is organized by Boxholm-Ekeby Ski Club and takes place at Boxholm’s ski stadium. It is a popular event for runners of all ages and abilities, with a beautiful and challenging course. More information and registration will be available closer to race day.
course_highlights: Scenic route around the Sjögarp area
Challenging 14 km course, with a course profile available
The race takes place at Boxholm’s ski stadium
additional: The race celebrates its 50th anniversary in 2026. Links are available to the invitation, race information, start list, and preliminary results from previous years. The course profile and a course map are available to runners. Gathering is scheduled for 09:30.

name: Hindås Trail
description: Hindås Trail is a running festival held on beautiful recreational trails in Hindås. Participants can choose between a 1 km race for children and 5 km or 15 km distances for adults. It’s a race for those who want to run fast, as well as a lovely run for those who prioritise the experience. At the finish, participants are treated to coffee and chocolate biscuits, and hot dogs and a more substantial fika are also available to buy. All proceeds go directly to Hindås’s popular cross-country skiing activities.
course_highlights: Beautiful recreational trails in Hindås
A 1 km children’s race on an easier course
Choose between 5 km and 15 km distances
additional: Hot dogs and a more substantial fika are available to buy at a good price. All proceeds from Hindås Trail go directly to the skiing activities. Coffee and chocolate biscuits are included after the finish. Hot dogs and a more substantial fika have been available for purchase. The proceeds go to Hindås Ski Club’s cross-country skiing activities.

name: Löfstad Slott Trail
description: Löfstad Castle Trail is an atmospheric trail race held in the autumn darkness around the historic Löfstad Castle. The race offers a unique running experience as participants run through the castle park, along forest trails and over unmarked terrain lit by headlamps. The event consists of two races: the Little Twilight Race for children in the park and Löfstad’s Darkest, a 7-kilometre night race for adults. Löfstad Castle Trail combines nature, history and community in a beautiful and challenging setting.
course_highlights: 7 km night race on gravel roads, trails and unmarked forest terrain
The course is marked with reflectors and course tape
Little Twilight Race: 1,000 metres in the park, with no timing
additional: Race bibs can be collected from 15:00 at the castle courtyard. Löfstad’s Darkest starts at 17:00 and requires a headlamp and trail shoes. The Little Twilight Race is a children’s race with no timing, and all participants receive a prize. The joint awards ceremony takes place after the races. On-site registration is available. Parking is available up to 500 metres from the castle. A headlamp is mandatory for the 7 km race, and trail shoes are recommended. The children’s race is untimed. The start and finish are at Löfstad Castle.

name: Kullamannen by UTMB
description: Kullamannen by UTMB is an adventure race along the rocky shores of Kullaberg and the Bjäre Peninsula on Sweden’s southwest coast. The races range from 22 km to 100 miles and offer challenging terrain through rocky hills, beech forests, and coastal trails. This is a tough and scenic trail-running experience that attracts adventurous runners from around the world. The races are part of the UTMB World Series and offer a unique combination of technical trails and spectacular views.
course_highlights: Technical singletrack on Kullaberg
Passage through 15 nature reserves and two hills (Ultra 100 Miles)
Coastal trails and beech forests along the Bjäre Peninsula
additional: The start and finish for Ultra 100 Miles and Sprint Ultra are in Höganäs, with bib pickup in Båstad. Drop bags are provided and can be collected at specific aid stations and after the finish. It is possible to transfer a registration to a shorter distance up to three weeks before the race. Minimum age varies by race, and parental consent is required for minors taking part in North Shore 20K. The event also includes an extensive schedule of activities during the week before the races. The race lineup includes, among others, 20K, 50K, 100K, and 100 miles. For the 100-mile race, bib pickup takes place at the EXPO in Båstad.

name: Kullamannen 100 miles
description: Kullamannen 100 miles is an extremely challenging A+ 100-mile race that takes you through 15 scenic nature reserves and two mountains in Skåne. The race starts in Höganäs and the course includes technical singletrack on Kullaberg, one of Sweden’s most popular nature reserves. After 66 kilometres, runners can refuel with hot soup before continuing north towards Ängelholm and Torekov, with the finish in Båstad. The race is known for its high DNF rate of 40–60% and the tough weather conditions in November, with Scandinavian coastal winds and long hours of darkness.
course_highlights: Passes through 15 nature reserves and two mountains
Technical singletrack on Kullaberg Mountain
Starts in Höganäs and finishes in Båstad, with a chance to refuel after 66 km
additional: The race starts in Höganäs, with buses departing from Båstad. Race bibs must be collected in person at the Expo in Båstad. Drop bags are provided and can be collected at the Båstad Aid Station and after the finish. Drop bags must be collected within two hours after the race ends. Bib collection by proxy is not permitted. The race is part of the UTMB World Series. Bibs must be collected in person at the EXPO in Båstad, with valid ID and a QR code. Participants receive an official UTMB World Series drop bag.

name: Walking Dead Ultra 100 Miles
description: Walking Dead Ultra 100 Miles is a challenging ultramarathon held in Paradiset Nature Reserve in Huddinge. The race offers a unique terrain experience, with scenic views and technical trails that test both endurance and mental strength. It is a well-regarded event for experienced ultrarunners seeking a long-distance challenge in a beautiful setting.
course_highlights: Running in Paradiset Nature Reserve with varied terrain
Technical trails and scenic views
A challenging 100-mile distance
additional: The race also offers 100 km and 65 km distances. According to the available race information, drop bags and toilets are available, along with water, tea, coffee and broth at Torpet Paradiset.

name: Finalloppet Göteborg
description: Finalloppet is western Sweden’s largest cross-country race, with a history dating back to 1968, and is organised by Göteborgs Skidklubb. The race offers several distances from 1.9 km to 19 km, all featuring varied terrain and challenging elements such as advanced trail sections. The race venue is at Skatås Motionscentrum in Göteborg, where the finish and services are located. The race is well organised, with clearly marked courses and water stations along the routes, and has classes for women and men in different age groups.
course_highlights: The 19 km course includes an approximately 2,500-metre advanced trail section
Courses are marked with orange arrows and kilometre markers in different colours for each distance
Water stations are located at several points along the longer courses
additional: Registration is via RaceID, with payment made at the time of registration. Start groups are used to spread runners out according to their stated running time. Startklar insurance can be purchased during registration. Registration for the Parvelbanan (approx. 250 m) takes place on race day. A sweep team is present on all courses. A doctor and medical staff are available at the finish area. Water stations, medical care and a sweep team are available along the courses.

name: Jätten Bule-löpet
description: The Jätten Bule Run is a traditional race organised by IFK Österbymo, set in the scenic, enchanting woodland around Österbymo. The race offers three distances: 10 km, 5 km and 2.4 km. Participants run on trails and gravel roads across varied terrain, with beautiful views. The start and finish are at Bulevallen. The race is sanctioned by the Östergötland Athletics Association, with chip timing. Changing rooms, refreshments and race-bib collection are available on site, making for a welcoming, well-organised race day.
course_highlights: The 10 km course winds through enchanting woodland on trails and gravel roads, with both climbs and descents
The 5 km course is a miniature version of the 10 km course, with a new route from 2024, and is marked in blue
The 2.4 km course follows the floodlit trail and is somewhat more challenging
additional: Race bibs can be collected from 09:00 at IFK Österbymo’s clubhouse by the start area. Bulis will lead the warm-up before the children’s race, at approximately 10:00. Timing is by chip. Changing rooms are available in the clubhouse. Refreshments, including coffee and hamburgers, are available at the start area; payment by Swish or cash. The start and finish are at the sports ground in Österbymo. The 10 km and 5 km distances are available both as running and walking.

name: Kilsbergsleden
description: Kilsbergsleden is a running race suitable for all levels, with distances from 5 km to 14.7 km. The race takes place in Karlslund Forest, starting and finishing at Karlslund Sports Centre in Örebro. The shorter distances run on lightly prepared forest terrain, while the longest course follows more natural forest trails with some rocky sections and climbs up and down an esker. The race is part of the Southern Svealand Running Series and offers both recreational and competitive categories.
course_highlights: Lightly prepared forest terrain and floodlit trails for 5 and 10 km
Natural forest trail with rocky sections on the 14.7 km course
The course climbs up and down an esker
additional: Race bibs can be collected at Örebro AIK’s clubhouse at Karlslund Sports Centre. Refreshments are available at the finish and at approximately 9 km, with water and cordial. Changing rooms and showers are available at Karlslund Sports Centre. Parking is available at Karlslund Sports Centre. Coffee and snacks are available for purchase on site. Prize money is awarded to the top three finishers in the competitive category for 14.7 km. The award ceremony takes place at 13:00 at the clubhouse. Refreshments are available at the finish and at approximately 9 kilometres.

name: Höstmilen
location: Sörsjön, Kolmårdsskogarna, Åby, Norrköping Municipality, Sweden
description: Höstmilen is a trail race along the paths between Sörsjön and Lillsjön, outside Åby, north of Norrköping. The race offers a challenging course through scenic terrain and an enjoyable experience for all participants. You can choose between a long course of 10.6 km, a shorter course of 5.2 km, and courses for children and young people. The shorter courses start and finish at Lillsjön. The event is organised by OK Kolmården, a ski and orienteering club for all levels and ages.
course_highlights: Trail running on paths between Sörsjön and Lillsjön
Scenic terrain in the Kolmården forests
Challenging courses of both 10.6 km and 5.2 km
additional: Registration closes on 29 October at 23:00. After that, you can register on 31 October from 11:00 to 14:00 at XXL and at the start area on 1 November. There are also classes for children and young people. Race director: Johan Malm. Parking and transport information is available on the website. If you have mild symptoms of illness, you should stay at home. The race has been held since 1971.

name: Landehof 4-Årstider Höstloppet 2026
description: Landehof 4-Årstider Autumn Race is an autumn orienteering competition organised by OK Landehof. The race offers challenging terrain with darkness, rain, stormy weather and slippery roots, creating a true autumn atmosphere in the forest. It is a traditional competition that attracts orienteers keen to test their skills in difficult conditions. Participants can enjoy an exciting experience close to nature in the Landehof area during autumn.
course_highlights: Challenging autumn terrain with slippery roots
Running in darkness and stormy weather
Orienteering close to nature in the Landehof area
additional: The start list will be published from Friday 30 October and updated until the final registration day. Live results and a results list will be available. QR codes are available to easily share the invitation and registration details with work or training companions.

name: Energiruset
description: Energiruset is a family-friendly evening race held in Mariebergsskogen in Karlstad. Participants can choose between two distances, 2 km and 5 km, and run, jog or walk with a headlamp along the unlit trails. The race is an energetic evening where participants defy the autumn darkness and share a sense of community and movement. After the race, all participants are treated to a sausage in a bun as a pleasant finish.
course_highlights: The race takes place in Mariebergsskogen, with parts of the course unlit
Option to run or walk with a headlamp on the 5 km distance
Family-friendly atmosphere with both a competitive class and open start times
additional: There is a 5 km competitive class with a provisional start time of 18:00. Other participants can use the course during the evening and start whenever they like within the stated time window. Headlamps can be purchased when registering.

name: Jämjöhalvan och Jämjöhallenstafetten
location: Jämjö, Karlskrona Municipality, Blekinge County, Sweden
description: Jämjöhalvan and Jämjöhallenstafetten are mass-participation races in Jämjö, with distances ranging from a children’s race to a half marathon. The race follows a fast, spectator-friendly loop course combining asphalt and gravel, and is a qualifying race for Göteborgsvarvet. Jämjöhallenstafetten is a relay in which four people run a half marathon together. The start and finish are near Jämjö Kunskapscentrum, and the event offers a sense of community for runners of all ages and levels.
course_highlights: Loop course: four laps for the half marathon, two laps for 10 km and one lap for 5 km
The course is 40% asphalt and 60% firm-surface gravel
Start and finish near Jämjö Kunskapscentrum, approximately 20 km east of Karlskrona
additional: Starts take place at different locations depending on the distance. The half marathon and relay start at 11:00, the 10 km at 11:10, the 5 km and youth races at 11:15, and the children’s race at 13:15. Relay teams can be mixed freely, and the baton handover takes place near the lap point. The course uses right-hand traffic, and runners are asked to keep to the right unless they are running fast.

name: Skanneloppet
description: Skanneloppet is an individual running race held in Åstorp, with three different courses suited to all ages and levels, from elite runners to recreational runners. The race starts with approximately 10 runners each minute and offers distances of 3.9 km, 7.6 km and 17.3 km. Competitors in race categories must be members of a club affiliated with the Swedish Athletics Association or an equivalent organization. Bib numbers can be collected on race day from 08:00 at Tingvalla nöjespalats in Åstorp. Medical assistance is available during the race.
course_highlights: Three courses: green 3.9 km, blue 7.6 km and red 17.3 km
Water stations along the course
Individual starts with approximately 10 runners per minute
additional: Bib numbers can be collected on race day from 08:00 at Tingvalla nöjespalats, Vramsvägen 9 in Åstorp. Those who register before 24 October will have their name printed on their bib. No on-site registration. Starts are individual, with approximately 10 runners starting each minute.

images.alt_text: IS Skanne-logotyp från inbjudan till Skanneloppet.
Löpare vid start och mål för Skanneloppet i Åstorp.

name: Höstrusket
description: Höstrusket is a running race held in Norra Djurgården in Stockholm, part of the Royal National City Park. Participants can choose from three distances: 10 km, half marathon and marathon, all on officially measured courses starting and finishing at Fisksjöängsvägen. The race offers a lovely blend of nature and culture amid the vibrant colours of autumn and is suitable for both beginners and experienced runners. It’s a perfect way to finish the running season or kick off winter training, with good support and encouraging pacers along the course.
course_highlights: Officially measured 10 km, half-marathon and marathon courses in Norra Djurgården
The course is mostly flat and fast, with asphalt and gravel surfaces
Two aid stations with water and sports drink along the course
additional: Start and finish at Fisksjöängsvägen, near Ropsten metro station. Race bibs are available at Runners’ Store in Stockholm and at the venue on race day. There are three start groups for the half marathon and four for the 10 km, based on expected finish time. Pacers are available for all distances. Drinks and something to eat are provided after the finish. Showers are available for a small fee at a nearby climbing centre.

name: Kroppefjäll Trailrun
description: Kroppefjäll Trailrun is a night race through the wild nature of Kroppefjäll in Dalsland, where participants run in teams of 2–3. The races offer several distances for all levels, from beginners to experienced trail runners, and provide a unique experience in which the same trails feel completely different in daylight and darkness. The courses are hilly and marked with reflective markers to make running in the dark easier. After the race, food is served, and participants can enjoy a sauna and a cold dip in the tarn.
course_highlights: 60% singletrack and entirely off-trail
Courses through hilly terrain, forest and natural trails
Courses are marked with reflective markers for running in the dark
additional: Participants start in teams of 2–3, with buses taking them to their respective starting points. Warm-up clothes can be left at the start and will be transported to the finish area. Food is included in the entry fee and served at the finish. After the race, participants can use the large sauna and take a cold dip in the tarn.

name: Iron Backbone Ultra
description: Iron Backbone Ultra is a challenging trail adventure along Järnleden, the backbone of Kristinehamn’s trail network. The race features technical trails and November darkness, creating a tough and exciting challenge for both mental strength and determination. Participants can look forward to a sense of community and an experience of nature in beautiful terrain. The race is organized by Topp & Dröm, who are passionate about making training and competition accessible and enjoyable for all levels.
course_highlights: Technical trails along Järnleden in Kristinehamn
Running in November darkness, with challenging weather conditions
A nature-focused trail adventure that tests mental strength and determination
additional: Mandatory equipment includes a headlamp, mobile phone with emergency number, first-aid kit, race bib, windproof jacket and reflective vest (except for the 16 km class). Recommended equipment includes a running backpack, fluids, warm clothing, extra energy and an emergency blanket. The race is limited to 150 participants and takes place in November. Participants must be properly equipped for the prevailing weather and terrain conditions.

name: Järndammsloppet 10 km
description: Järndammsloppet is an annual cross-country race organised by IFK Sala at Järndammsstugan in Sala. The race offers distances of 10 km and 5 km, as well as a 1 km children’s race without timing. The start and finish are at Järndammsstugan, which has changing rooms and showers. It is a family-friendly event with prizes for the winners in each category and raffle prizes. Coffee and refreshments are available for purchase after the race.
course_highlights: Cross-country race starting and finishing at Järndammsstugan
Distances of 10 km, 5 km and a 1 km children’s race without timing
Changing rooms and showers are available
additional: The 1 km children’s race starts at 11:00, without timing, and all participating children receive prizes. The 5 km and 10 km races start at 11:30, with prizes for the winners in each category and raffle prizes. Changing rooms and showers are available at the event area.

name: Dammekärr Dirt Dash
location: OK Alehof klubbstuga, Dammekärr, Nödinge, Ale Municipality, Sweden

tiers.label: tier_1
tiers.description: Deltagande är gratis för medlemmar i OK Alehof

tiers.label: tier_2
tiers.description: Övriga betalar 199 kr för tre deltävlingar

description: Dammekärr Dirt Dash is a trail running series in Dammekärr, organised by the orienteering club OK Alehof. The competition consists of three races with a combined points total, and participants can choose to run one, two or all three races. The courses run through hilly forest terrain and offer three distances: 1.5 km, 3.5 km and 7.0 km. After finishing, runners can enjoy a hot sauna and refreshments in the clubhouse, creating a welcoming atmosphere.
course_highlights: Hilly forest terrain around Dammekärr
Short course (1.5 km) on the floodlit trail
Longer courses (3.5 km and 7.0 km) require a headlamp
additional: Timing is done using a SportIdent chip, which can be borrowed on site if you do not have your own. All races take place in the evening. After the race, a hot sauna and refreshments are offered in the clubhouse, including coffee, cordial and homemade baked goods.

name: Skatås Mörkaste
description: Skatås mörkaste is a night trail race held in the Delsjö nature reserve in Gothenburg. Runners tackle winding narrow trails, rocky outcrops and wider paths in the dark, following hundreds of reflectors illuminated by their headlamps. There are two distances, approximately 7 km and 12 km, with challenging climbs such as Slättåsryggen, Brudarebacken, Getryggen and Knipeflågsryggen. After the race, participants are served hot soup and bread, and can enjoy a non-alcoholic bar with a pleasant selection. Skatås mörkaste is also a popular after-work event, with a friendly atmosphere and a chance to socialise.
course_highlights: Run along winding narrow trails and rocky outcrops in the Delsjö nature reserve
Hundreds of reflectors along the course guide runners in the light of their headlamps
Challenging climbs such as Slättåsryggen, Brudarebacken, Getryggen and Knipeflågsryggen
additional: Race bibs can be collected at Pölder Sport on the Wednesday and Thursday before the race, or at the event venue from 17:00. The timing chip is attached to the back of the race bib. Runners under 15 must run with an adult. Umara sports drink is available once on the 7 km course and twice on the 12 km course, as well as after the finish. Changing rooms and showers are available in limited numbers. SM Sport sells trail-running equipment at the venue. Hot soup and bread are served after the race, including vegetarian/vegan options. A non-alcoholic bar is available, with cash and Swish payments accepted. The start and finish are at IFK Göteborg Orienteering Club’s facility in Skatås. A headlamp and trail shoes with good grip are recommended.

name: Sätila Trail
description: Sätila Trail is a trail race around lake Lygnern with start and finish on the lake shore in Sätila, organised by the orienteering club OK Räven. The distances are 5, 10, 22, 43 and 85 km on paths, forest roads and gravel roads through old-growth forest, past lakes, through the old cultural landscape of Äskhult and over Texelberg. The longest course, Lygnernslingan at 85 km, goes all the way round the lake. The next edition is on Saturday 13 November 2027.
course_highlights: Lygnernslingan, 85 km around the whole of Lygnern
Through the old farming landscape of Äskhult and over Texelberg
Five distances from 5 to 85 km
additional: Registration for 2027 opens on 1 December 2026. The 85 km is capped at 150 runners and closes one week before the race; the other distances stay open until race day. Prices until 30 September/from 1 October: 85 km 1,050/1,300 SEK, 43 km 850/1,000 SEK, 22 km 450/600 SEK, 10 km 300/400 SEK, 5 km 200 SEK. Start and finish are at Lygnevi IP, and the 85 km has a drop bag at Äskhult.

name: Gränsö Trailrun
description: Gränsö Trailrun is a coastal trail race through Gränsö Nature Reserve, starting and finishing at Gränsö Slott in Västervik. The race offers two distances, 8 km and 15 km, both featuring varied, scenic courses with trails, cliffs and oak pastures. It is a race for both beginners and experienced runners who want to enjoy nature or challenge themselves. All finishers receive a medal, and there are aid stations along the course. Gränsö Trailrun is a welcoming, family-friendly experience, with the opportunity to combine the race with dining, spa and an overnight stay at the castle.
course_highlights: More than 90 percent trails and walking paths on both distances
Coastal nature reserve with seaside trails, cliffs and oak pastures
Start and finish at beautiful Gränsö Slott, set in a castle environment
additional: There is an option to choose the Fun Run without timing. The event centre opens at 09:00 at Gränsö Slott. The 8 km race starts at 11:00 and the 15 km race at 11:20. There is one aid station on the 8 km course and two on the 15 km course. All finishers receive a medal. You can combine the race with lunch, a day spa, dinner or an overnight stay at Gränsö Slott. Energy and hydration stations are available along the courses: one on the 8 km course and two on the 15 km course.

name: Pop up Run Svartedalen
location: Bottenstugan parking, Svartedalen, Stenungsund Municipality, Sweden

tiers.label: tier_1
tiers.description: Pris: 300 kr, lättare lunch, dryck och kaka ingår.

description: Pop up Run Svartedalen is a wonderful trail-running experience where you can discover the wilderness-like landscapes of Svartedalen, with winding forest trails, mirror-still lakes and hilly terrain. The run covers a distance of 12 km and is divided into 2–3 pace groups. Several stops are made along the way to enjoy the views and the special atmosphere in one of western Sweden’s most popular nature areas. After the run, a light lunch with a drink and cake is served at the wind shelter, creating a lovely sense of community and an energetic morning in nature.
course_highlights: Winding forest trails through deep spruce forests
Mirror-still lakes and moss-covered areas
Hilly terrain with mountain-like scenery
additional: The run is divided into 2–3 pace groups. Meet at the Bottenstugan parking area. Meeting time: 10:00 at the Bottenstugan parking area. Participants are divided into 2–3 pace groups.

name: FalkTrailen

price_tiers.distance: Dam och Herr 5 km och 10 km

tiers.label: tier_1
tiers.description: Anmälningsavgiften är 250kr för herr- och damklasserna.

tiers.label: tier_1
tiers.description: Barnloppet kostar 20kr som skänks till välgörenhet

description: Falktrailen is a trail race organised by Falkenberg Allstars. The race offers several categories for both women and men over 5 km and 10 km, as well as untimed children’s races. Most of the course follows lovely narrow trails, and trail shoes are recommended. Refreshments are available for purchase during the event, and prizes are awarded to the top three in each category. Part of the entry fee goes to charity supporting families with children in financial hardship in Falkenberg.
course_highlights: Most of the course follows lovely narrow trails
Trail shoes are recommended, but regular running shoes are also suitable
Untimed children’s race, with a prize for every participant
additional: The children’s race starts at 10:00 and is not timed. Registration for the children’s race closes at 9:45. The regular categories are capped at 350 runners. Late registration is available subject to space, and it is not possible to register late on site. 20 kr of each entry fee goes to the Swedish Church’s “Family Diaconia” fundraiser. Start times are listed as between 10:30 and 13:00.

name: Mörkertrail
location: Garphyttan National Park, Lekeberg Municipality, Örebro County, Sweden
description: Mörkertrail is a unique 10 km trail race run in total darkness in Garphyttan National Park in Lekeberg Municipality. Participants run with only a headlamp for guidance along a reflective-marked course that features both technical sections and easy-to-run trails, with plenty of elevation gain. The race offers a special atmosphere where runners can experience the deep darkness, tranquillity and sounds of the forest. After crossing the finish line, participants can enjoy a grilled sausage by the fire in a cosy setting. The start and finish are at the national park car park, and the race starts at 17:00.
course_highlights: 10 km trail race in total darkness with headlamps
Reflective-marked course with both technical and easy-to-run trails
Course with plenty of elevation gain on the edge of Kilsbergen
additional: Race bibs can be collected from 16:00. There will be a short briefing 10 minutes before the start. No on-site late registration. Start and finish at the entrance/car park to Garphyttan National Park. The car park has limited spaces, so please carpool. There is an outdoor toilet but no changing facilities. Bringing your own headlamp with a fully charged battery is mandatory. Sausage and a drink are included after the finish.

name: Kristianstad Trail
description: Kristianstad Trail is organized by Härlövs IF in the Bockeboda area outside Kristianstad and is promoted as an autumn highlight for trail runners. The race offers several distances, making it accessible to both experienced trail runners and recreational runners. Preliminary race information and courses are published on the website, along with information about course previews ahead of the event. Organizer pages and the registration link are collected on the race website.
course_highlights: Running in Bockeboda Forest — woodland terrain near Kristianstad
Several distances: approx. 25 km (25–26.4 km), 12 km (12–12.9 km) and 5 km (5.3–5.7 km), depending on the measurement method
Course distances are listed with variations depending on different measurement methods
additional: Registration: the page mentions individual and group registration. The website mentions insurance and includes a registration link for a previous year’s edition (Registration for Kristianstad Trail 2025). Course previews have also been held ahead of the race, and late registration has previously been announced as available via Racezoo. The race has a long tradition in Kristianstad, and information about this year’s edition is available in news articles and race information on Härlövs IF’s website and the RaceID page.

name: Nyårsloppet
description:
For the 43rd time, Vallentuna Friidrott invites everyone—from elite athletes to recreational runners and children—to take part in a winter race on the streets and squares in central Vallentuna. Participants and spectators may be met with challenging ice, slushy snow, wonderfully crisp winter weather or a fast asphalt course.
Nyårsloppet is a great way to get a little active before the New Year’s meal and the year’s reflections. And as some people say: “What you do on New Year’s Eve sets the tone for the rest of the year!” So take the opportunity to get active, bring a friend and run or jog around the course.

name: Craft Idre Fjällmaraton
description:
Become unbeatable
We believe everyone has the right to feel unbeatable at some point. Not in relation to anyone else, but in relation to yourself. Unbeatable because you achieved something you didn’t think was possible. Because you dared to do something you didn’t think you could. Because you ventured into unknown territory and won. You won over that little voice telling you that you can’t.

name: Nyårsloppet Vallentuna
description:
The New Year’s Race is a perfect way to get active during the days between Christmas and New Year. For the 42nd time, Vallentuna Friidrott is inviting runners to take part on New Year’s Eve, with everyone from elite athletes to those who prefer a more relaxed pace. A winter race can mean challenging conditions or fast asphalt—we never know until race day. Keep an eye on the weather forecast and read our information. Statistically, conditions have been favourable for running in most years, as the results from previous years show.

Above all, the New Year’s Race is a lovely way to get together to round off the old year and have something to talk about at the celebrations later in the day.

You’re welcome too—we’ll see you there!
additional: Please remember that the New Year’s Race is a winter race, and conditions can vary from year to year. In some years, spiked shoes may be recommended.

name: Sollentuna Winter Marathons
description:
Welcome to SWM!
Experience the adrenaline of running on ice! Sollentuna Winter Marathon offers three spectacular races in one day, with Arena Edsvik creating a festive atmosphere and Edsberg Castle, dating back to the 1630s, providing a royal setting.

NEW! - Winter X 10K - SOLO
A fast-paced 10K winter race on and around the ice of Edsviken, with up to 4 km of spectacular ice running before you sprint to the finish at Arena Edsvik. The race starts at 12:00!

Winter Half Marathon 21K - TEAM & SOLO
A beautiful and challenging half marathon on and around Edsviken, with up to 7 km of spectacular ice running. The race starts at 12:00!

Winter 21K - CANICROSS
All runners with dogs get the chance to experience magical ice running with their four-legged best friend! Only 50 spots for dog teams—first come, first served. Flexible start between 11:45 and 12:00.

Winter Kids Run by Team Rynkeby Täby 1.5K
A fun race for children born in 2014 or later, on wintry roads around Edsberg Castle. All proceeds go directly to the Swedish Childhood Cancer Fund through Team Rynkeby Täby. Start at 11:00.

Together, we support the Swedish Childhood Cancer Fund

name: STHLM Trail Marathon
description:
A warm welcome to the second edition of STHLM TRAIL MARATHON
All races take place on a very scenic course, approximately 15 km long. Each lap will offer you nearly 500 metres of elevation gain. Expect beautiful views and challenging running, mostly over hilly terrain and mostly on trails, sometimes off-trail, but also on a couple of gentler sections where you can stretch out and run for a few hundred metres.

New for 2026
• Be on the start line as early as April! This time we’re holding the event in early spring, so mark 18 April in your calendar now.
• Kids Trail, a free race for our younger runners (born in 2014 or later).
• Hjärnloppet, a virtual race lasting 18 days, where the entire entry fee goes directly to Hjärnfonden and vital research into epilepsy.
• Course preview runs. On two occasions, we’ll run through the first and second parts of the course.
• Virtual running sessions in the Heyey app to help you stay in shape all the way to the start line in April.

What’s not new for 2026
• The course, a challenging and very scenic route in the area around Lake Flaten.
• Sprint and Ultra, two trail races that challenge you a little extra.
• Grit, the ultimate test, which we don’t think anyone can complete. If you prove us wrong, you’ll win both honour and fame, as well as some prize money.
additional: All information on the organiser’s website

name: Billingen Trail
description:
We invite you to enjoy running on Billingen. This year, the start and finish will be at the Stadium in the Billingen Recreation Area.
The long course is just over 47 km with approximately 930 metres of elevation gain. It goes all the way around northern Billingen, along beautiful trails by the edge of the mountain. As a runner, you’ll experience varied terrain, including deciduous forest, mountain ravines, meadows and spruce forest, as well as beautiful views across the landscape from several places. The surface varies from easy-to-run sections and approximately 6 km of asphalt to some more challenging parts.

The middle-distance course, 21 km, follows the northern section of the Billinge Trail and has approximately 500 metres of elevation gain. The course includes a mix of trails, meadows and roads.

Our shortest distance, 12 km, has just over 200 metres of elevation gain and follows trails of varying difficulty, with some short sections on roads.

Information about the courses and markings may change.

Start:

47 km, 10:00, Stadium, Billingen Recreation Area, Skövde.
21 km, 10:45, Björnasäter, Lerdala. Bus departs from the Billingen Recreation Area at 10:05.
12 km, 11:30, Stadium, Billingen Recreation Area, Skövde.

Finish:

At the Stadium, Billingen Recreation Area, Skövde.

All finishers cross the finish line at the stadium.

name: Isaberg500
description:
Isaberg 500 is the race we love running ourselves and the foundation of the entire trail weekend. It’s a perfect mix of trails, hills, sweat and tears that brings to mind spectacular races in both the Swedish mountains and the Alps. Isaberg 500 also features switchbacks, long, enjoyable downhill stretches and fantastic views. In between, you can enjoy winding trails through enchanting forests. Isaberg 500 includes at least 500 metres of elevation gain and is perfect for anyone training for a mountain marathon or similar race.

NEW FOR 2025!
When Isaberg500 started, Jättestigen was a big talking point. A few years later, it was closed due to the risk of landslides. In 2025, Jättestigen returns as part of Isaberg500, but under a new name — Jättetrappan...

Isaberg500 is a race in the Outnorth Trail Tour 2025.
course_highlights: Trail race with varied trails and hills, with a technical character reminiscent of races in the mountains and the Alps
Multisport around the Isaberg summit: kayaking, mountain biking and trail running — Solo and Duo categories
Isaberg Gravel: a circuit of approximately 45 km, starting and finishing in Åsenhöga; Elite/up to age 50: 3 laps, older riders/sport recreation: 2 laps, recreational: 1 lap
additional: Contact GI by mobile at +46 703 815 118 or email at gimulti@gmail.com. Organisers: GI Folkestad and Martin Jepson. Guided rides for cycling groups can be booked; the organisers have ready-made routes that can be adapted to the group’s needs. Main distance: approximately 10.5 km (Distans Trailtour); Kids Trail: approximately 2 km with approximately 150 metres of elevation gain; start time: Sunday at 12:00; location: Isaberg/Anderstorp; contact: niklas@isabergtrail.se.

description: Rambo Mosse Night Trail is a unique trail race through the fascinating natural surroundings of Rambo Mosse Nature Reserve in Mölndal. The race, which is just over 11 km long, takes place at dusk, with headlamps and a course marked with reflectors, offering a special and challenging running experience on forest trails. The start and finish are at Herkulesgården, where participants can enjoy a sauna, showers and warming soup in the clubhouse after the race. The race is limited to 400 participants and includes a medal and awards for the top finishers in the women’s and men’s categories.
course_highlights: Just over 11 km on forest trails marked with reflectors
A gently undulating course featuring a mix of forest, bogs and rocky outcrops
Run by headlamp, starting and finishing at Herkulesgården
additional: Maximum 400 participants. All participants receive a training hat from Ullmax (value: SEK 149). Aid stations with water and Umara sports drink at approximately 4 km and 8 km, and after the finish. Electronic timing with a split time. After the race, showers, a sauna and warming soup with bread and a drink are available in the clubhouse. Race bibs can be collected the day before or on race day. Recommended equipment includes a headlamp with sufficient battery life and trail shoes with good grip. Parking is limited; public transport is recommended. Start and finish at Herkulesgården. Registration is via RaceID from 1 September and remains open until 25 November or until all 400 places are filled. The entry fee includes refreshments, soup after the finish, a training hat, a medal for all finishers, and access to changing rooms, showers and a sauna.

description:
What is Backyard Ultra?
Backyard Ultra takes place on a marked 6,706-metre loop, and each participant has one hour to complete it. A new start takes place at the top of every hour, and as long as you can complete the loop within an hour, you remain in the race. You win by being the most enduring and ultimately getting to run one final lap alone! A fun race and concept with a very welcoming, community-minded atmosphere, where many participants set their distance records!

Whether you’re aiming for a personal best, want to run at a relaxed pace or simply enjoy the atmosphere, UppLoppet is for you. In addition to the race, we’re offering several enjoyable activities for both participants and spectators. Welcome to celebrate movement, health and community with us on National Day!

description: Ängelholms IF invites you to a great evening of running at Kullavallen! You are very welcome!

description: Whether you want to set a personal best over five kilometers or simply feel like running an easy-to-run race, now you have the chance to run Värmland’s fastest 5K. The race starts and finishes right in the center of Kil, at Gröna Torget. A warm welcome!

description:
For the fifth year in a row, Burlövsloppet will be held on September 5 in conjunction with Burlövsfesten, right in the center of Burlöv! Anyone can take part, regardless of age, ability, or pace—movement, community, and joy are at the heart of it.

Lilla Burlövsloppet is free; the other races cost SEK 200–250.

description:
Vreta SoMK welcomes you to a cross-country race in the Olstorp terrain!

Gather your friends, colleagues and teammates, and come to Olstorp. There are races for everyone, big and small.

name: VAIS-loppet
description:
The VAIS race is organised by Växjö AIS every spring and autumn.

The race follows a hilly recreational trail through the Fylleryd Nature Reserve, and you can choose between two distances: 4.4 kilometres and 8.4 kilometres.

Both courses start together at 18:30 by the VAIS cabin. After the races, we round things off with coffee and refreshments.
additional: The race is free for members of Växjö AIS. For non-members, the entry fee is 50 kronor.

name: Ultra Caballo Blanco Suecia
description:
Only the 100-mile race starts on Friday (08:00); the 100 km and 50-mile races start on Saturday (06:00).
All three races have their own routes (they have nothing in common with CBMR, which takes place on the same day). The 50-mile and 100-mile races have some staffed aid stations, which are also shared with the 100 km race, which has its own stations as well. The 100-mile race is virtually entirely unsupported, apart from a few unmanned water stations. You also pass a well-stocked country store and a church with water and toilets.
All three races offer the option of a drop bag.
The courses are completely unmarked, so you navigate using a downloaded GPX file...
additional:
We don’t have paper cups, so bring a cup!
Hot food, drinks, coffee and cake are served after the finish.

The entry fee includes 120:-, which is sent to a children’s race in Urique, Mexico!

name: Caballo Blanco Memorial Run (CBMR)
description:
This is the route that Caballo Blanco (aka Micah True) and I ran on 2011-09-26, when he was visiting Sweden at my invitation. In spring 2012, we received the news that he had died. We then organised a memorial race on 2012-09-22. It became a tradition, and eventually the race offered 1, 2 or 4 laps of the route, which is approximately 11 km and has approximately 150 metres of elevation gain.
See also Ultra Caballo Blanco Suecia — an ultra race held at the same time.
An article I wrote quite a while ago, when we introduced the 50-mile race:
https://redsports.se/CBM/TheStory.html
additional:
The 4-lap race starts at 12:00, while the 1- and 2-lap races start at 15:00.
Please note that you must bring your own cup/mug.
The entry fee includes drinks, energy products, and a hot meal with coffee and cake after the race.

name: GUM - Gotland Ultramarathon
description:
One of Sweden’s most beautiful ultramarathons. The race starts at 9:00 at Hallshuk in northern Gotland, and the course heads south along the coast, with the sea on your right all the way to Visby. The route is approximately 50 km, with very varied terrain.

There is also a Half-GUM (28 km), starting at 11:00 in Lickershamn.

name: XC-race Linköping
description: Linköping XC-race is an annual cross-country race organised by Linköpings OK in Vidingsjön, Linköping. The race offers a marked 5 km loop through varied terrain, including trails and marshland, and is open to both recreational runners and competitive classes. Participants can choose between 5 km, 10 km for men and women, and a 5 km recreational class. The 10 km races cover two laps. The event is known for its challenging, muddy terrain, and the start and finish are at Vidingsjö Motionscentrum.

name: Västerås Marathon
description:
NEW RACE 2026

Västerås Marathon offers three distances — 42 km, 21 km and 10 km — on a flat, fast course through the heart of the city and along the beautiful shores of Lake Mälaren. The course is a loop course, with 10 km per lap.
Experience the joy of running in a well-organised race for all levels.

The race is for everyone who enjoys running, from beginners to elite athletes. All ages and paces are welcome, and generous time limits will be set for completing the race.

A warm welcome!

name: Kilterrängen
description: Are you among those who prefer trails to asphalt? Whether you’re a curious beginner, a recreational runner, or an elite runner, Kilterrängen is for you. Starting and finishing at Frykstahöjden in Kil, this 16 km trail race ends with a few tough kilometres full of hills, including the notorious ski slope. The course is just as suitable for running at full speed as for jogging, walking with poles, or hiking. You can also choose to run 6 km, with the same tough finish as the longer course.

A Backyard race lasting under 6 hours.

name: Löparfesten
description:
The running festival offers several different races, with something for everyone!

Whether you’re looking to set a personal best in the half marathon or prefer a walk with good friends, there’s a great race to choose from!

EKO ½Maran is for experienced runners, FORMTOPPEN Milen is a wonderful challenge, and the slightly shorter Here We Go 5an is for happy recreational runners or those who prefer to run fast but short. For those who want to take it a little easier, perhaps bring walking poles or a stroller, or simply enjoy nature, there’s Here We Go 5an – Promenad!

There are also races for younger participants—Papricaloppet—for everyone up to 12 years old! We also have Rulleruset for everyone with a disability! At Rulleruset, you can choose between a shorter 1.4 km race and a slightly longer 5 km race!

As we said, there’s something for everyone!

name: Å-stadsloppet
description:
Å-stadsloppet runs through both Örebro’s neighborhoods and scenic areas such as Rynningeviken and Wadköping.

The 5, 10 and 21.1 km courses have all been officially measured by federation course measurer Bertil Sundin.

name: Uppsala Marathon
description:
UPPSALA MARATHON
17 OCTOBER 2026
Through centuries of history – one step at a time
MARATHON • HALF MARATHON • MARATHON RELAY
Celebrate 10 years with us!
Challenge yourself and experience one of Sweden’s most popular races in beautiful autumnal Uppsala. Run the marathon or half marathon, or gather family, friends or colleagues and take part in the marathon relay.
Uppsala Marathon is turning 10!
Over 42,195 metres, the course takes you through some of Uppsala’s most historic, scenic and remarkable surroundings. From the castle and Carolina Hill to the River Fyris, the city centre and leafy green spaces – a unique combination of running, history, culture and a festive atmosphere.
Whether you’re an experienced marathon runner or taking part for the first time, you’re warmly welcome to help write the next chapter in the race’s history.
All participants are invited to enjoy a post-run gathering, and all finishers receive a technical T-shirt and this year’s exclusive 10th-anniversary medal.
More information and registration:
https://www.uppsalamarathon.se/

description: Fjällmaraton Sälen by EQPE is the trail adventure for those who love experiences, running and beautiful nature. Choose to run 42 km, 21 km or 10 km, and the children can also take part in Barnens Fjällmaraton. Along mountain trails, paths, boardwalks and gravel roads, nature will challenge you on your way to the finish and the After Run at Experiumtorget in Lindvallen. Fjällmaraton Sälen by EQPE is a deluxe running challenge! Join us and experience the joy of running in the mountains!

name: Änglamilen
description: Änglamilen is a long-established fun run in the heart of Ängelholm. Participants experience the town, the sea and the forest all in the same 10 kilometres. The 5 km race begins with a lovely run through the park in the charming Hembygdsparken. After approximately 2.7 km, the course crosses the Rönne River and continues along the beautiful riverside path in Nybroskogen. Finally, the course turns back across the river, with a sprint to the finish at Tullakrok. The 10 km course starts the same way as the 5 km route, but turns north after about a kilometre. Runners are treated to beautiful views over Skälderviken and its harbour, with Kullaberg visible in the background. After approximately 7.7 km, the courses join again, and runners can enjoy the beautiful riverside path in Nybroskogen.
additional:
The deadline for standard registration is 18 May, but late registration is available until one hour before the start of each race.

Stay up to date by following us on Facebook and Instagram
https://www.facebook.com/anglamilen
https://www.instagram.com/anglamilen_angelholm

We’ll fill the stadium with runners of all ages, and welcome you whether you’re an elite runner or a recreational runner.
